clue.text: Confused accountant, afraid of anything electrically induced

indicators.note: confused letters are mixed up, so the accountant's letters and the word afraid are jumbled together

explanation.surface: A muddled accountant is scared of anything run on electricity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confused' could describe the accountant, but it signals the jumble; 'accountant' stands between the indicator and 'afraid', so its abbreviation joins the pool.
explanation.definitionFit: Faradaic describes current produced by induction, named after Michael Faraday's work on electromagnetism.

clue.text: Extension makes it possible for lady to accommodate a divorcee

indicators.note: to accommodate is to house someone, so the lady's name holds the other piece within it

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse, such as a divorcee

explanation.surface: A woman agrees to let her former husband stay in the extension.
explanation.definitionFit: An annexe is a building added on to a main one, a kind of extension.

clue.text: In my dream our love affair went on and on

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit inside the words my dream our, running across them

explanation.surface: Someone dreams of a romance that never ends.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'dreAM OUR'; 'went on and on' is surface colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Amour is a French borrowing for a romance, especially a secret one.

clue.text: Right to enter guilty plea

explanation.definitionFit: Admission means both the permission to go in somewhere and a confession of guilt.

clue.text: Vehicle parked on the left of the shelter

parts.note: port is the left-hand side of a ship

explanation.surface: A car has been left parked beside a shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: A carport is a roofed but open-sided cover for a parked vehicle.

clue.text: Appalled because some wag has taken too many liberties

indicators.note: some means only part of the words wag has taken is used, the letters lying within them

explanation.surface: A joker has gone too far and people are shocked.
explanation.definitionFit: Aghast means filled with horror or shock.

clue.text: Permit to take two points away from a flier

indicators.note: take, with away from, says some letters are removed from the bird
away from completes the instruction to remove the compass points from the flier

parts.note: a swallow is a bird, something that flies
S and W are two compass points, south and west

explanation.surface: A licence is needed to remove a couple of points from a pilot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take ... away from' removes S and W (south, west) from SWALLOW.
explanation.definitionFit: To allow is to let something happen, a synonym of the verb permit.

clue.text: Where top people get drunk before going straight?

indicators.note: before places the word for drunk in front of the word for straight

explanation.surface: Senior figures get drunk and then sober up.
explanation.definitionFit: High-level describes the senior ranks of an organisation, where its most important figures sit.

clue.text: Ought the queen to take responsibility?

parts.note: ought to and should mean the same
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Should Her Majesty accept the blame?
explanation.definitionFit: To shoulder a burden is to accept it as one's own duty.

clue.text: Tell a student where he should be

definitions.text: a student where he should be

explanation.surface: Someone tells a pupil where to go.
explanation.definitionFit: To inform is to tell; a pupil should be in form, that is in class, a British term for a school class.

clue.text: One girl I converted to the faith

indicators.note: converted means changed in form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A young woman has been converted to a creed.
explanation.definitionFit: A religion is a system of belief and worship, such as a creed.

clue.text: Former wife goes to the newspapers and gets given nothing but coffee!

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse

explanation.surface: A divorcee goes to the papers and receives nothing but a cup of coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: The usual spelling is espresso; expresso is a recognised variant.
explanation.definitionFit: Expresso is a variant of espresso, a strong black drink made by forcing steam through ground beans.

clue.text: Note taken by young Bill without any thought

indicators.note: taken by means held inside, so the note goes into the boy's name

parts.note: Willy is a pet form of William, Bill when young

explanation.surface: A small boy called Bill is handed a note without thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting wildly means acting recklessly, without restraint or reflection.

clue.text: Opinions given from high places

explanation.surface: Opinions are delivered from lofty heights.
explanation.definitionFit: Points of view are opinions; also, literally, high lookout spots offering vistas.

clue.text: Dry men took first manuscript paper

parts.note: to parch is to dry out

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the word took

explanation.surface: Thirsty men were the first to take up old manuscripts.
explanation.definitionFit: Parchment is treated animal skin used as a writing material for manuscripts.

clue.text: Scottish islanders, alternatively bounders taking Scottish name

indicators.note: taking means holding inside, so the bounders enclose the name

parts.note: cads and bounders are both dishonourable men
Ian is a Scottish form of John

explanation.surface: Some island Scots, or perhaps some rogues, have a Scottish name.
explanation.definitionFit: Orcadians are natives of Orkney, the islands off northern Scotland.

clue.text: Exploit a break out which got some publicity

indicators.note: which got means the escape received something inside it

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, a bit of publicity

explanation.surface: A prison breakout made the news.
explanation.definitionFit: An escapade is a daring or mischievous adventure, an exploit.

clue.text: Very large, and universal too

explanation.surface: Something is both enormous and all-embracing.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomical means huge, as in astronomical costs, and also relating to the universe and its stars.

clue.text: Service to the elderly offered by a physiotherapist perhaps

definitions.note: names the thing offered: a treatment given by a physio, a noun phrase

parts.note: age means old people collectively, as in youth and age

explanation.surface: A physiotherapist looks after older patients.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbing and kneading the body is a treatment a physiotherapist commonly gives.

clue.text: One backward German boy just about survived lions

indicators.note: backward means the assembled letters are read in reverse order
just about here means closely surrounding, so the boy goes round the German word

parts.note: ein is the German for the number one, which the clue's 'One' supplies

explanation.surface: A German lad barely lived through something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One ... German' is the German word for one; 'just about' wraps the boy round it and 'backward' turns the result. In the Bible Daniel survived the lions' den.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical prophet was thrown into a den of big cats and emerged unharmed.

clue.text: Cleaner used to be a lady

parts.note: was is the past of be

explanation.surface: A cleaning woman was once a lady.
explanation.definitionFit: A washer is a person or machine that cleans things by washing.

clue.text: Made iller by stream

indicators.note: made means formed into something else, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone was made sicker by drinking from a stream.
explanation.definitionFit: A rille is a variant of rill, a small brook or channel.

clue.text: Team with genuine stars moving about

definitions.note: adjective sense: relating to the stars

explanation.surface: A team boasting true stars is on the move.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidereal means measured by or relating to the fixed celestial bodies.

clue.text: Small civet with floppy ears seen round the south

indicators.note: seen round means the rearranged ears wrap around the letter for south
floppy means loose and shapeless, so the letters of ears are rearranged

explanation.surface: A little civet with droopy ears is spotted down south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'floppy' makes RASE from EARS; 'seen round' puts S inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The rasse is a small Asian civet-like mammal.

clue.text: Came back, not at all well, but carrying a flower

indicators.note: back means the word for unwell is turned around

explanation.surface: Someone returned sick, but holding a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: The camellia is an evergreen shrub with showy blooms.

clue.text: Sailors lie back when coming down the rope

definitions.note: a participle phrase for the verb's action of descending

indicators.note: back means the word lie is reversed

explanation.surface: Sailors lounge about while descending on a line.
explanation.definitionFit: To abseil is to descend a steep face by sliding down a fixed line.

clue.text: Calm down and pay up

explanation.definitionFit: Settle means to become quiet and also to clear a debt or bill.

clue.text: Festival towards the last half of July held facing the rising sun

indicators.note: last half of takes the final two of the four letters of July

explanation.surface: A festival late in July is held looking east.
explanation.definitionFit: Easterly means towards the east, where dawn breaks.
